newsitem.title: USA: US oil industry says AAA plea would hurt consumers.
newsitem.headline: US oil industry says AAA plea would hurt consumers.

text.p: Big oil companies said Friday a plea by the American Automobile Association for the U.S. government to make refiners shore up their gasoline inventories to ease gasoline prices was misguided.
The American Petroleum Institute, which represents oil companies, said that to build up gasoline inventories, refiners would have to divert supplies from the market.
"Reducing the current supply of gasoline available to motorists, given the current level of deamnd, would mean higher prices, not the lower ones that AAA wants," API said.
"In summary, AAA is advocating actions that would boomerang and hurt American consumers -- not help them," it said in a statement.
An Energy Department spokesman said Friday that the department was aware that inventories were low, but it was unlikely to get involved in the gasoline market.

API said gasoline prices were 15 percent above last year's levels not because inventories were low but because crude oil prices had surged due to strong economic growth and higher energy demand worldwide.
